steps.content: The sand constructing the scene disperses. Your soul tumbles with a thud, fitting perfectly back into your body. You look around. To your surprise, you find yourself back in your own office.

Irrheia is right across from you, having just withdrawn her hand from the hourglass. The Aurum Secretum device shakes intensely, the swirling sand making a howl-like noise. You can still see irregular red light spikes pulsing and fading like heartbeats.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Did you really think the story would unfold smoothly according to your script, culminating in a classic, clichéd "happy ending"?

You instinctively activate the shackles. When the surroundings seem stable with no disruption, you confirm this isn't yet another layer of illusion, but reality. You lift your gaze to look Irrheia directly in the eyes.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Then you've certainly underestimated me. Perhaps you should spend more time studying The Secret History of the MBCC published by that tabloid.

Irrheia is neither flustered nor angered by your sarcasm. She leans forward slightly against the desk, casually brushing her cascade of hair once, seemingly unconcerned about your confrontation mere seconds ago.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Oh? What makes you say that?
Her amused tone reveals she isn't genuinely asking for an answer, but simply taunting you loftily, demanding that you respond to her challenge. And you're ready to take her on.

options: Because it would have been too predictable.

choices.text: Because it would have been too predictable.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I never believed in that tragic past you showed me. After all, you let me restart too many times, enough for me to explore every corner, noticing the elements in your script that resembled other Sinners' stories.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If you didn't draw inspiration from The Secret History of the MBCC, then someone must have fed you with those stories, resulting in this script full of recycled ideas and familiar plot twists.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: My, that's a rather harsh critique. Did you not enjoy this story? That's surprising. Isn't this exactly the kind of stereotypical narrative that everyone seems to love?

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Dark family drama corrupts the innocent girl to become a Sinner, turning her into a madwoman in the attic, who is then redeemed by the wise savior and reclaims her own happiness. The gimmick, the melodrama, the heartwarming ending. It has everything.
Irrheia pretends not to get your meaning, but you refuse to dance around the subject with her any longer.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This has nothing to do with whether I enjoyed it or not. I'm not your customer, and I'm not going to write you a review for cashback. I came to you seeking an honest conversation, but you tried to deceive me with a clichéd story you've cobbled together.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: As I've told you, my reality has always been stranger than fiction. I can spot the slightest incongruity in even the best story. And if this is your carefully crafted script, then maybe you're in fact not that good of a creator.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Though I shouldn't be surprised. Of course an Eastside white-collar worker with an ordinary lifestyle would believe that her own boredom is the only authentic reality. Your script is boring because you are a boring person surrounded by boring things.
This isn't the first time Irrheia has tried to deceive and manipulate you with her custom-made illusions and stories. You're deliberately provoking her, mocking her frivolous love for novelty.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: ...Heh, perhaps you're right. Perhaps this is the root of everything.

She simply waves her hand. The notebook opens on its own, countless pages filled with cursive writing fluttering and interweaving as they turn rapidly. Surrounded by all these different universes, Irrheia acknowledges your criticism thoughtfully.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: I noticed the bottleneck long ago. I turned out new scripts, tried new themes, cast new NPC actors, and even deliberately guided the actions of those more "creative" players... but nothing worked.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: The thrills in my scripts grew fewer and faded faster. Everyone's choices became predictable... I discovered that even the one thing that could pull me from that void of emptiness was beginning to fail.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: I certainly didn't want to return to that numbing existence, so I began searching for new variables, and I managed to find you. But perhaps... you're just a timely, pleasant surprise, while the real problem lies elsewhere.

One by one, pages detach from the notebook and scatter everywhere, then rearrange themselves in some unknown order before slipping back into the spine. You suspect Irrheia might be taking inventory of her past creations.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Nothing new under the sun. I've witnessed countless people let their choices be shaped by their experiences. The same applies to my own works as well, hence the loops and repetitions... the recycled ideas and clichés...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: By bottleneck, do you mean your scripts were declining in quality and no longer felt thrilling to you or provided escapism? Did you start creating these scripts for this reason in the first place?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The manipulation and real-time adjustments in your scripts are just extensions of your creative process, aren't they? But is the person sharing all this with me the real you, or just another improvised character you've created, another "witch" in your story?

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Looks like you've become quite the murder mystery game expert. Indeed. A rich girl who was used as a human blood bag for years, then returned with her superpower for revenge? Such a trendy character concept. I might have made it up myself.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Perhaps the real me is actually just a nine-to-five office worker who writes scripts, occasionally putting on costumes and acting out roles just to earn my performance bonus.
Irrheia smiles noncommittally, seemingly pleased that you're following her rhythm. But you won't fall into her rhythm.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yes, I could certainly take guesses, but why would I? I don't care which parts of you are real and which are not. As Chief of the MBCC, I'm only concerned with your safety under Mania, and whether you're using that power to influence others.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Just like you only care about these so-called thrills. They're the reason you create your scripts, manipulate events, and exhaust yourself trying to escape the MBCC. As long as something keeps you entertained, you couldn't care less when exactly I saw through your act.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And now, I've successfully planted the shackles within you. From now on, whenever you abuse Mania with harmful intent, I'll know immediately and be able to intervene. This is what I want, and I've already achieved it.

You open your palm, revealing crimson light flickering between your fingers. Irrheia stares at it, seeming to contemplate your true intentions behind all this. From this moment, the dynamic between you finally begins to shift.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Fine, fine, put away your victory trophy. No need to flaunt it in my face. Though... I don't mind it when you're being a show-off. It's fun to see you like this, my dear Chief.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm not like you. I don't wear different masks. Whether inside or outside your scripts, I'm just myself. That interrogation might have been staged, but my words weren't.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I promised that if you allowed me to give you the shackles, I would grant you freedom. I'll keep my word. I'll even help you break free from what's been eating away at you all this time. Boredom.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: In truth, I've always preferred to build trust with Sinners, and that begins with mutual understanding. I called you to my office for this reason. We need to clarify what we each want and be completely honest with one another.
You gesture with an open palm toward the notebook placed between you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Before you dragged me into that scenario of yours, I thought we'd already achieved this. We discussed how you used the emotions that erupted in your scripts to fill the emptiness of your reality.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: The more extreme the content, the more vibrant the medium, the emptier ordinary life feels once the screen goes dark. I was tired of those packaged experiences that never reached the core or the flesh, even though I was the one creating them. I needed something that could truly move me.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: So I played the Witch, making my customers fight for their lives, cry out in pain, find their courage on my stage... The stories were fake, but the emotions were real. For some fleeting moments, I felt ignited by their emotions, borrowing their racing heartbeats to feel alive again.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Yes, all stories eventually end, which is precisely why one should seize the present experience. The virtual thrills and connections may fade away, but isn't that better than spending an entire lifetime numbed by emptiness and absence?
You repeat Irrheia's words, raising your eyes to meet hers.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I don't fully agree with your philosophy, but I understand you and trust your motives aren't dangerous. I thought that script... the one about being honest about your past, offered a deeper form of connection.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But it is just another script you've cobbled together. No one knows how much of it is real. I'm curious, what are you really looking for in all this? Do you truly believe these repetitive scenarios can give you what you need?
Irrheia freezes momentarily, then lets out a quiet laugh. She taps a finger between the pages of the notebook, then slowly withdraws it, like treating a toy she's tired of.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: A script is just a script. As for its meaning to me... isn't that already clear to you? It's full of possibilities and can be replayed endlessly. Once I introduce new variables, it can generate new excitement and save me from boredom.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yes, it is clear to me. But what's clearer to me is that they're becoming less effective for you. Have you considered how much longer these predictable scenarios can deceive your clients? Or how much longer they can deceive you?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: When you finally realize you've completely run out of inspiration and nothing stimulates you anymore, what will you do then? What will become of your scripts?

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Yes, what should become of them...

Under your persistent questioning, Irrheia lowers her eyes to the hefty notebook and falls into deep thought. You don't interrupt her, but you can sense Mania flowing and swirling, gathering strength in dark undercurrents.

Suddenly, she throws up her hand, and the surging Mania splashes in all directions. You can almost feel its spiraling trajectory like a sandstorm, reminiscent of what you've experienced in WhiteSands, as white grains whip past your cheeks! You barely stop yourself from activating the shackles!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What are you...!

But you stand transfixed by the scene before you. The Mania isn't whipping up sand grains, but the pages containing whole universes from the notebook. They swirl around Irrheia, being crumpled and torn apart!
She's actively withdrawing the Mania power she has infused into the notebook! The pages aren't being destroyed by outside force, but by their owner!

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: These scripts are merely props, and creating them is just one way I amuse myself. Now that I know I'm not even that good at it, and I have you, a constant variable who always manages to surprise me...

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: So what if I stop making them?
Irrheia picks up the notebook's empty shell and casually tosses it behind her, clearly relishing the undisguised shock on your face.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Don't look so surprised. You know perfectly well that I only write these scripts for fun... But these thrills are fleeting. Once they get old, no one cares about them anymore.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: So what if I tear up these scripts that no longer entertain me? What does it matter if I find something even more exciting and stop creating altogether? The only thing I ever want is to pursue new thrills.
You collect yourself, not wanting her to see you waver as your mind races, weighing whether you should see her opinion, even more radical than you anticipated, as a good or bad thing.
Meanwhile, Irrheia watches you with obvious interest, savoring every reaction of yours with joy.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: My dear Chief, are you feeling nervous right now? Don't worry. After seeing so many Sinners' stories, I understand why you're always probing each Sinner's inner world, searching for their deepest obsessions...

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Because obsessions are our anchors. Surveillance and perception aren't infallible. You prefer to nip the problems in the bud, but for things beyond your control, you can only rely on these anchors to restrain and limit them.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: People with fewer, more abstract obsessions are more dangerous to you, like me. You've been provoking me all this time, pushing me to admit my scripts have become useless... but my scripts are my anchor.

The carefree, almost languid-looking Witch finally bares her fangs, closing in relentlessly with razor-sharp words, making your heart clench. No wonder she's dubbed the Witch of Rewind. She knows human nature like a supernatural being who's been alive for centuries.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Without it, what else can you use to control me? Unless... you already know the answer. Go ahead then, say it. What's your trump card? What's this antidote you've found?

But as you look up at her eyes, unusually bright with excitement, you feel unexpectedly calm. What glimmers in her eyes is clearly anticipation, not hostility. She doesn't want to defeat you, but is only curious about your response in a plight.

Just as she did in all those scripts and loops you've been in before, she casually flicks her fingertips while relentlessly pressing her questions. What she seeks has always been the same: change, thrills, surprises.

She's right. People with fewer obsessions are harder to control. But someone with desires as simple and direct as hers doesn't actually care how you deliver what she wants. Stories inevitably end, but experiences alone are real.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Just as I know your past was never a mediocre script that needed rewriting, neither is this reality. The one trapped in loops isn't me. It's you. What imprisons you in endless boredom isn't reality, but the loops themselves.

Irrheia tilts her head back slightly, as though she's just read an absurd plot twist. Her lips curve into a smile, though she doesn't speak. A more genuine, expectant smile gradually reaches her eyes, tinged with both playful mockery and curiosity.

The scripts, the manipulation, and the narrative control are all just the Witch's attempts to stave off boredom. Yet these safe, "controlled" experiments only trap her in a vicious cycle of increasing monotony.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Interesting. Do continue, my dear Chief. Let me see what other fresh theories you've developed.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I believe you already know. These scripts which you can rewrite, enrich, and reset may be safe and convenient, giving you endless opportunities to explore, but no matter how many times you try, they can never give you that soul-stirring excitement you're seeking.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Because choices you can undo at will are never truly impactful. They can't crack your shell or leave any lasting impression. Deep down, you already know that some things are precious because you only get one chance at them.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Didn't that Outlander's death shake you precisely because of this reason? If it had merely been the "permadeath" of a character, would it still have affected you so deeply?

For the first time, all expressions vanish from Irrheia's face. This should make it appear stiff like a mask, but with that thin veneer of a smile stripped away, you realize this might be her true, pensive face.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Seeking thrills in these scripted cycles will never be truly satisfying. If you are determined to escape this boredom that ensnares you, I suggest you shed your armor, step out of these cycles into reality, and experience the world firsthand.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You could even leave Eastside behind, travel to distant places, and see other parts of the world, like the Outlands. It may not be easy or entirely safe, but I guess danger is rarely boring, isn't it?

Her fingertips tap against her cheek. Her gaze sharpens for an instant, then quickly softens again. Her smile has returned almost imperceptibly, but it's like still water disturbed by the wind, ripples spreading underneath.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: ...How strange. Compared to all the cycles I've experienced, your life has surely been shorter and less substantial, yet you consistently do and say the most unexpected, truth-revealing things. Why is that?

options: Perhaps because reality is always stranger than fiction.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: During my first murder mystery game, you asked me if my complex experiences had made me unable to understand ordinary people's boredom and aspirations. I think there may be some truth to that.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I've certainly had some... extraordinary encounters that most people will never experience, or even imagine. That's how I learned that stories need to be logical, but reality doesn't. The truth is, reality always catches you off guard.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I wouldn't call all these experiences pleasant, but I've certainly never been bored. If that's the kind of life you're after, I believe nothing can stop you from changing your path now and stepping out of Eastside, this cocoon you've been living in.
Irrheia listens quietly, her fingers still resting against her cheek. The rhythmic tapping pauses for a moment.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Stories need to be logical, but reality doesn't... So reality always triumphs over stories. Is that why those of us who seek solace in stories are doomed to emptiness and ruin?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Not at all. I don't think reality is inherently better than fiction. Sometimes people need the safe, accessible escape that virtual entertainment provides. What I'm trying to say is, if simple stories no longer satisfy you and instead drive you toward the extremes...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Then perhaps the real issue lies in your reality itself. Stepping out to experience more of reality might help you find what you're truly seeking. And when you eventually return to stories, those real experiences can enrich them.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Oh? So you'd let me return to stories and scripts? You were the one who called my scripts mediocre and goaded me into abandoning them all. Now suddenly you're not worried about how dangerous and uncontrollable they are?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I am. Even the scripts you find unbearably dull are still dangerous enough for ordinary people with weaker minds.
At this point in the conversation, her tone no longer sounds provocative and has become more playful, so you also decide to be frank.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But that doesn't mean I don't care about your quality of life as a Sinner. I want ordinary people to live safely, but I also want you to be happy. That's the real reason I think you should go out and explore.
You sigh, rummage through your desk, and pull out a plain notepad normally used for recording key details during interrogations. You slide it across to Irrheia.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'd even encourage you to record what you experience. They could make excellent material for your work. I never expected you'd actually tear up your notebook... So please, take this one instead.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If you trust me and choose to step out of your shell into the real world... then I think you'll find a notebook useful. Remarkable events blur together easily in memory, but stories last forever once they're told. And don't worry, you'll have plenty of readers at the Bureau.
Irrheia stares at the notepad, her expression darkens momentarily, then she suddenly smiles. It carries a hint of mischief, as if she finds your suggestion amusing.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: You really are full of surprises. I have to admit, when you first walked into my shop, I never expected you'd be so... reckless, but fun. What's in it for you, encouraging me like this?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: No matter who you really are, I know your sole motivation is seeking twists and escapism. And now, I want you to break free from the endless cycle and the prison of boredom too. Our goals are the same.
She doesn't respond. The interrogation room falls into momentary silence as you wait patiently. Finally, Irrheia leans forward, reaches for the notepad, and opens it.
You expect her to examine it for some hidden trick, but she simply turns to the first page, takes one of your pens, and writes a single line.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: "Real twists and surprises are found in reality."
The elegant cursive writing trails in a long final stroke, like the opening line of a new script. You can't help but look up at her.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Since you've brought me so many surprises, I suppose I'll try this theme you've suggested. Even though I love chaos and surprises... perhaps you're indeed the one true variable in my life?

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: As for that notebook... I'll leave it with you. You've written the opening act of this script, and for the rest... I'll continue writing it until I've experienced the vast world you spoke of.

Yet another lengthy field assignment is finally over. You drag your exhausted body and push open the door to your lounge, ready to black out. But before you sit down, your eyes are drawn to an open notepad on the desk. It doesn't belong to you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The writing, the format... A script? Has Irrheia returned?!

You flip through several pages and discover they contain an incredibly detailed account of your recent field assignment. The writing is lyrical and accurate, capturing even your exact words and the decisions you made.
There's no signature on the script, but the familiar cursive handwriting clearly belongs to Irrheia.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, I was just coming to find you... Copies of this script seem to be circulating throughout the Bureau. They're being distributed as a murder mystery game prop. It's now a popular form of entertainment among Sinners.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Although the sensitive information has been censored or altered, the Intelligence Security Department has still flagged it as a Level B risk. Also, a note appeared on my desk with Sinner Irrheia's handwriting. It says...

It's been a while, my dear Chief. I've explored all the places you recommended before returning to DisCity. Syndicate, WhiteSands, Fraser, the farlands... they were indeed wonderful, but still not as interesting as being by your side.

I hope you've kept my room for me. After skipping work to cooperate with your investigation and taking this extended unpaid leave, my boss has already fired me. There's no place for a jobless person in Eastside, so you'll have to take responsibility for that.
You fold up the note and shake your head with a smile.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I knew she would come back. As for this script... fine, let her be, seeing as no real sensitive information was leaked, and the circulation is limited within the Bureau.
